svg.title: Average Ticket Decides Whether a Service Fee Stays Above Water
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-cash-discount-ticket-math; chapter number: 4; title: Average Ticket Decides Whether a Service Fee Stays Above Water; subtitle: Signature debit cost as a share of the sale versus the fee charged; chart type: stacked_comparison; total range: Debit cost of about 1% to 6.4% of the sale against a 3% to 3.99% service fee; buckets: label: $5 ticket debit cost; low: 6.4; high: 6.4; notes: Fixed 30 to 32 cents swamps the fee; quote a per-item fee such as 59 cents.; label: $10 ticket debit cost; low: 3.2; high: 3.2; notes: Shepherd says a $10 ticket goes negative 20 basis points at 3%.; label: $30 ticket debit cost; low: 1.0; high: 1.0; notes: Inside the $25 to $70 sweet spot with the fattest ISO markup.; label: Service fee charged; low: 3.0; high: 3.99; notes: Corporate reward cards near 2.5% interchange squeeze this on high tickets.; caption: Regulated signature debit runs 22 cents plus 5 basis points, roughly 30 to 32 cents all-in, so small tickets sink a percentage fee.; assumptions note: Cost percentages are James Shepherd's examples; FTx POS found over 80% of its card transactions flagged as debit.; note: Sources include James Shepherd of CCSalesPro and FTx POS.
